title: Less is More: Hop-Wise Graph Attention for Scalable and Generalizable Learning on Circuits
problem: Graph neural networks struggle with scalability on large circuit graphs and fail to generalize to new, unseen circuit designs, limiting their practical application to large-scale, complex circuit problems in EDA.
motivation: GNNs are popular for circuit analysis and optimization tasks but have scalability and generalization limitations that prevent real-world deployment on complex designs.
method: HOGA pre-computes features for each circuit node at different neighborhood distances (hops—1 step away, 2 steps away, etc.). A gated attention mechanism then learns which distances are most important for each feature, making these decisions independent of how the circuit graph is wired. This independence allows the model to work on new circuit designs it has never seen and enables efficient training across multiple computers.
key_novelty: Gated attention on hop-wise features that learns what matters independent of the circuit's structure.
contributions: HOGA architecture combining hop-wise features with gated self-attention for circuit representation learning
46.76% error reduction in QoR prediction compared to conventional GNNs
10% improvement in functional reasoning accuracy on unseen gate-level netlists
Linear training time scaling with distributed computing resources
